original_question: Let G be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Does G remain anisotropic over every finite extension K/F whose degree is not divisible by any prime in the set S(G) of homological torsion primes of G?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 7.3 (the generalization of the Springer problem from involutions to anisotropic absolutely almost simple linear algebraic groups).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact paper target: an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group G over a field F, anisotropic over F, and the question whether anisotropy is preserved after passing to every finite extension K/F whose degree avoids the primes in S(G). This is precisely the content and scope of Problem 7.3.
missing_details: Make explicit that F is an arbitrary base field and that G is an F-group.
Spell out that remain anisotropic over K means the scalar extension G_K = G ×_F K is anisotropic over K.
Define S(G) stand-alone, not just by name: in the paper it is the set of homological torsion primes in the sense of Serre, listed type-by-type in Table 7.
State the degree condition in the precise form [K:F] is prime to every prime in S(G).
To stay paper-faithful, note that this question is posed as the group-theoretic generalization of the odd-degree anisotropy question for involutions discussed immediately before it in Section 7.
refined_question: Let F be a field, and let G/F be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Let S(G) denote the set of homological torsion primes of G in the sense of Serre, equivalently the set listed by Dynkin type in Table 7 of the paper: S(A_n) is the set of prime divisors of n+1; S(B_n) = S(C_n) = S(D_n) = S(G_2) = {2}; S(F_4) = S(E_6) = S(E_7) = {2,3}; and S(E_8) = {2,3,5}. Is it true that for every finite field extension K/F with [K:F] prime to every prime in S(G), the base change G_K remains anisotropic over K?
justification: The draft unmistakably targets Section 7, Problem 7.3: the paper introduces it immediately after the unitary-involution discussion as a generalization of Problem 7.1, using exactly the language of anisotropic absolutely almost simple linear algebraic groups and the set S(G) of homological torsion primes. The only real gap in the draft is that S(G) is not defined in a stand-alone way; the paper supplies that definition through Serre's notion and Table 7.
